stories.whyItMatters: Pada can leave jail while his appeal is pending, though his conviction stands. The order follows earlier bail grants to other convicts in the case.

stories.headline: Tonk residents say streetlights removed after BJP candidate lost Rajasthan panchayat poll
stories.dek: The MLA linked to the candidate denies involvement, as the BJP's Panchayati Raj results last week were its weakest in Zila Parishad polls in at least three decades.
stories.summary: Residents of villages in Rajasthan's Tonk district allege about 50 streetlights were removed after BJP candidate Priyanka Sharma lost a Panchayat Samiti ward by 751 votes. Niwai MLA Ram Sahay Verma denies any link to the removal.
body: About 50 streetlights in villages in Rajasthan's Tonk district were allegedly removed within a day of a BJP-linked candidate losing a Panchayat Samiti election, residents told The Indian Express. The residents have protested.

The lights were in Ward No. 2 of Piplu Panchayat Samiti. Priyanka Sharma, wife of the personal assistant to Niwai MLA Ram Sahay Verma, lost the ward as a BJP candidate to her Congress rival by 751 votes.

Villager Suresh Kumar said the lights had been installed 20 days before the election, without residents having to approach any candidate. He said a vehicle from the electricity department arrived within a day of the results and began taking them down.

According to Kumar, workers said the lights had been installed without the department's permission. "This directly indicates that once the candidate Priyanka Sharma lost the election, she had the lights uninstalled," he said. He added that workers would not leave the lights in place for two days despite a wedding in his family.

Residents of Hanifganj and Kumharon ki Dhani also objected. One resident said public amenities should not be withdrawn because a candidate lost, and that villagers had asked the electricity department to explain the timing and circumstances of the removal.

Verma rejected the allegation as false. "No streetlight was installed by anyone linked to me," he told The Indian Express. He said candidates sometimes install lights or do other civic work during elections, and that whatever happened was connected to "some local leader" and not to him.
The Indian Express report did not include a response from the electricity department or from Sharma.

The Tonk episode follows the Panchayati Raj results announced last week. The Indian Express reported that the ruling BJP recorded its worst Zila Parishad performance in at least three decades and its worst Panchayat Samiti result in 16 years. In the Panchayat Samiti polls, the gap in vote share between Congress and BJP was 5.37 percentage points, the third-highest in 30 years.
The Quint described the results as the BJP's worst rural poll loss in 30 years and asked whether the Congress was on its way back. Its full text was not available.

stories.headline: Belgian national strike halts flights and transport as thousands march in Brussels
stories.dek: Prime Minister Bart De Wever's five-party coalition remains split over budget cuts, with King Philippe urging him to reach a deal as soon as possible.
stories.summary: A national strike against planned austerity measures stopped all air traffic at Brussels and Charleroi airports and disrupted public transport on Monday. Tens of thousands marched in Brussels while the prime minister's coalition remained divided over the budget.
body: A national strike against planned government budget cuts halted all flights at Brussels Airport and Charleroi and disrupted public transport across Belgium on Monday, as tens of thousands of people marched through the capital.

Air traffic controllers' action meant no flights took off or landed at Brussels Airport in Zaventem between 07:00 and 21:00 local time. Airport spokesperson Jeffrey Franssens said 404 flights could not be operated, affecting more than 50,000 passengers.

At Charleroi, which serves low-cost carriers including Ryanair, all flights were listed as "scheduled" regardless of departure time. One passenger told broadcaster RTBF she had received no warning and learned of the shutdown only on arriving at the airport.
Underground services in Brussels were also halted. Schools and other public services faced disruption.

Florence Faure, a French passenger who had flown in from Beijing, told Reuters her connection to Paris Charles de Gaulle was cancelled. "Since our luggage was supposed to go on to Paris Charles de Gaulle, we didn't even collect it," she said.
Philippe Naime, a teacher who joined the march, told Reuters: "Quite simply, no more money is being invested in education, and people are left to fend for themselves."

Bert Engelaar, head of the FGTB union, said the government had alternatives to "dismantling the social protection system". He called for "a genuine wealth tax, fair taxation, and the elimination of tax loopholes". Ann Vermorgen of the CSC union criticised plans to cut bank holidays that fall on weekends.

Prime Minister De Wever leads a five-party coalition. The socialist party Vooruit has refused to endorse plans agreed by the other four, seeking higher taxes on the rich and smaller cuts to pensions and health spending.

De Wever met King Philippe on Monday for the third update since the impasse began. The royal palace said the king regretted the lack of significant progress and encouraged the prime minister to persevere. The king had earlier this month declined De Wever's resignation.
France 24 reported that De Wever set a new year-end deadline for the coalition to agree a cost-cutting budget or face collapse.

stories.background: King Philippe declined De Wever's resignation earlier this month, giving him more time to negotiate. Strikes have hit Belgium repeatedly in recent months as the government tries to agree a budget to cut borrowing costs.
stories.whyItMatters: More than 50,000 air passengers were affected at Brussels Airport alone, and the budget dispute will determine whether De Wever's coalition survives.

stories.dek: Gadi Eisenkot, asked by Israel's president to try to form a coalition, said the overnight attacks on Palestinian villages endanger lives and damage Israel's security.
stories.summary: Israeli political figures, led by Gadi Eisenkot, condemned overnight raids by extremist settlers on West Bank villages on Sunday. Separately, NPR reported that Palestinian ambulance drivers describe Israeli checkpoints as dangerous obstacles.
body: Israeli political leaders, led by Gadi Eisenkot, condemned overnight raids by extremist settlers on Palestinian villages in the West Bank on Sunday, with several calling the attacks "Jewish terrorism".

Mr. Eisenkot, a former military chief, has been asked by Israel's president to try to form a new governing coalition after elections last month. The New York Times described him as the man seeking to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

"Extremist groups that set fire to vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel's national security and foreign relations," Mr. Eisenkot said. He called the raids "acts of Jewish terrorism, and we must call them by their name."

The Wire, which reported the story as a condemnation of suspected settler attacks, described them as suspected. The New York Times said the raids were part of a spate of violent incidents over the weekend. The material available did not include casualty figures or details of any arrests.

According to the Times, Israel is under increasing international pressure to address years of mounting violence by Jewish settlers against Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. Critics say Mr. Netanyahu's government has taken little action to rein in the attacks. The government's response to Sunday's condemnations was not included in the reporting available.

Separately, NPR reported on conditions for Palestinian ambulance crews in the occupied West Bank. Drivers must pass Israeli checkpoints and road closures to reach hospitals, and they describe the checkpoints as dangerous obstacles to their work.
Rights groups told NPR that wait times at the checkpoints have spiked and that medics have been attacked.
keyFacts: Gadi Eisenkot condemned the settler raids on Sunday, calling them 'Jewish terrorism'.
Israel's president has asked Eisenkot to try forming a coalition after last month's elections.
The raids targeted Palestinian villages in the West Bank overnight, with vehicles and homes set on fire.
Rights groups say checkpoint wait times for Palestinian ambulances have spiked and medics have been attacked.
stories.background: The New York Times reported that Israel faces increasing international pressure over years of mounting settler violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. Critics say Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government has done little to curb it. Israel held elections last month, and the president has asked Mr. Eisenkot to try to form a government.
stories.whyItMatters: The condemnations put settler violence at the centre of Israel's coalition talks. Palestinian medics say movement restrictions also affect how quickly the injured and sick can reach hospitals.

stories.headline: Houthis say Saudi-led coalition strikes on Hodeida telecoms sites killed 17
stories.dek: The Houthi telecommunications ministry said the attack also wounded 11 and cut phone and internet services for tens of thousands; Saudi Arabia has not commented.
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthis said coalition airstrikes on telecoms facilities in Hodeida on Monday killed 17 workers and wounded 11. Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment, and AFP could not verify the claims.
body: Yemen's Houthis said on Monday that a Saudi attack on the Red Sea governorate of Hodeida killed 17 people and destroyed several buildings.

The Houthis' telecommunications ministry said coalition airstrikes hit telecoms facilities, killing 17 workers and wounding 11 more. It reported the "total destruction" of administrative buildings, staff housing, a mosque and other sites.

"This has led to the complete destruction of these facilities (and) the disruption of telecommunications and internet services", the ministry said, adding that tens of thousands of people were affected.

The group's military spokesman, posting on X, said a separate coalition attack in Lahj governorate, in the southwest, targeted buses and transport vehicles and also caused casualties. He gave no figures, according to the reports.
Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on either incident. AFP said it was unable to independently verify the claims.

A day earlier, the coalition said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched towards Saudi Arabia's western Red Sea coast. The region holds major oil installations, which Houthi fighters have attacked in recent weeks, along with airports and military sites.

On Sunday, Houthi media released a video that appears to show weapons depots the group said it seized a month ago near the coastal city of Mocha, after government forces withdrew. The footage, carried by the Houthi news agency Saba, shows dozens of containers of missiles, shells and drones that the group claims were made in the United States.

Crates of ammunition in the video carry labels indicating they passed through Dammam in eastern Saudi Arabia. Saba called the shipment the largest ever seized by the Houthis and said it would let them "fight the enemy for years".
According to the latest UN toll, fighting in Yemen since July has left more than 1,600 people dead and over 300,000 displaced.
keyFacts: Houthis say 17 telecoms workers were killed and 11 wounded in Hodeida on Monday, November 23.
Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment; AFP could not verify the claims.
Houthis also reported a coalition attack on buses and transport vehicles in Lahj.
UN: over 1,600 dead and more than 300,000 displaced since July.
stories.background:
Yemen has been in civil war for more than a decade. The Iran-backed Houthis control large parts of the country, including Hodeida, and fight a Saudi-led coalition that backs the internationally recognised government.

The country was drawn into the wider US-Iran conflict in July, when a truce between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government unravelled.
stories.whyItMatters: Tens of thousands of people in Hodeida are affected by disrupted telecoms and internet services, according to the Houthi ministry, while fighting since July has displaced over 300,000 people, the UN says.

stories.headline: Namma Metro ridership rises 12% and fare revenue 49%, but net loss widens to ₹1,710 crore
stories.dek: BMRCL's finance costs rose to ₹1,793.03 crore in 2025–26 from ₹560.01 crore a year earlier, outpacing gains in income, its annual report shows.
stories.summary: The Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited reported 310.49 million passenger journeys and fare revenue of ₹1,125.58 crore in 2025–26. Its net loss still widened to ₹1,710.13 crore from ₹1,405.67 crore, as finance costs climbed sharply.
body: The Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) recorded a net loss of ₹1,710.13 crore in 2025–26, up from ₹1,405.67 crore the year before, even as ridership and fare income grew, according to its 20th annual report.
Passenger journeys rose 12.29% to 310.49 million from 276.51 million. Average daily ridership increased to 8.51 lakh from 7.57 lakh, a rise of 12.42%.

Fare-box revenue climbed 49.36% to ₹1,125.58 crore from ₹753.59 crore. Non-fare revenue, from leasing, advertising, parking and electric vehicle charging, rose 61.02% to ₹88.51 crore from ₹54.97 crore.

The corporation attributed the fare growth mainly to higher ridership after the 19.15-km Reach-5 Yellow Line between RV Road and Bommasandra opened in August 2025. The network's highest single-day ridership, 10.82 lakh passengers, came on August 14, 2025, when fare revenue reached a record ₹4.58 crore.
Gross income rose about 46.2% to ₹1,624.62 crore from ₹1,111.59 crore. Operating expenditure, excluding depreciation and finance costs, increased to ₹823.69 crore from ₹665.50 crore.
Finance costs, however, rose to ₹1,793.03 crore from ₹560.01 crore. Depreciation was ₹725.36 crore, against ₹576.79 crore in 2024–25. The loss before tax was ₹1,717.46 crore.

BMRCL reported a profit before interest and depreciation of ₹800.93 crore, compared with ₹446.09 crore previously. It also reported an operational profit of ₹417.42 crore and a cash profit of ₹209.66 crore.
The report said trains ran with 99.85% punctuality. It also cited tokens, Smart Cards, QR tickets and National Common Mobility Cards as aids to passenger convenience.

BMRCL has not recommended a dividend for the year because of the losses. Its authorised share capital was raised from ₹16,000 crore to ₹22,000 crore after shareholders approved the move in September 2025, and paid-up capital was ₹15,987.72 crore on March 31, 2026.
keyFacts: Net loss for 2025–26 was ₹1,710.13 crore, against ₹1,405.67 crore in 2024–25.
Fare-box revenue rose 49.36% to ₹1,125.58 crore.
Finance cost rose to ₹1,793.03 crore from ₹560.01 crore.
Record single-day ridership of 10.82 lakh came on August 14, 2025.
No dividend recommended for 2025–26.
stories.background: BMRCL is carrying out Phase 2, Phase 2A, Phase 2B and Phase 3 expansion projects, involving spending on infrastructure, land acquisition, construction and rolling stock. The Yellow Line between RV Road and Bommasandra opened in August 2025, and the Pink Line from Kalena Agrahara to S.G. Palya was inaugurated on November 13, 2026.
stories.whyItMatters: The figures show the metro's operating income covering its running costs while borrowing and depreciation from network expansion keep the corporation in loss, with no dividend for shareholders.

stories.headline: Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma resigns over elephant drive; Forest Department halts operation
stories.dek: The Congress legislator submitted her letter to the Speaker's office on Monday; a meeting with Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy is set for November 30.
stories.summary: Congress MLA Nayana Motamma submitted her resignation to the Karnataka Assembly Speaker's office on Monday, protesting the operation to drive wild elephants out of Hassan. The Forest Department has since stopped driving the herds after 38 elephants entered Mudigere taluk.
body: Congress MLA Nayana Motamma of Mudigere submitted her resignation to the Karnataka Legislative Assembly Speaker's office in Bengaluru on Monday, protesting the Forest Department's operation to drive wild elephants out of Hassan district.
An official confirmed that the office had received the letter but said it had not been accepted. Motamma left without answering questions from the media, The Indian Express reported.

The department has meanwhile halted the drive. Chikkamagaluru Deputy Conservator of Forests K.T. Boraiah said on Monday that senior officers had directed that no driving be carried out that day, after 38 elephants entered Mudigere taluk. He said there would be no driving for now, as the coffee harvest is under way.

The herds are split into two groups about 2-3 km apart, one at Baradahalli and the other at Makonahalli. About 60-70 personnel are monitoring them, with drones used for tracking. Schools in nearby areas have been given a holiday. Boraiah asked planters not to burst crackers or send workers near the animals, and urged people not to go out of curiosity or film videos.

The operation began after two people died in Belur taluk within three days last week. The department brought in 12 kumkis, or tamed elephants, and deployed over 350 staff, with more than 100 police personnel assisting. Officials first captured two tuskers said to be responsible for the deaths and moved them to Nagarahole.

Hassan district in-charge minister K M Shivalinge Gowda ordered the herds driven towards the Bhadra Tiger Reserve. He said Hassan has no forest cover for them. "There is enough forest area in Bhadra wildlife," he said, adding that the Centre must also step in to protect forest areas.

On Sunday, Motamma and fellow Chikkamagaluru district Congress MLAs T D Rajegowda (Sringeri) and H D Thammaiah (Chikkamagaluru) said at a joint press conference that moving the elephants would worsen human-animal conflict in their region. "They have not taken us into confidence before launching the drive. I don't have to answer the government, but I have to answer the people," Motamma said. She alleged the drive was carried out unilaterally although a consultation with MLAs was scheduled for November 30.

Residents also oppose the move. Many gathered in Mudigere town on Monday and asked the government to withdraw the elephants from the taluk. Former MLC M.K. Pranesh said the taluk would call a Mudigere bandh if the government did not respond to the demands.

The Forest Department said the herd moved on its own from Makonahalli towards the 874-hectare Tatkola Reserve Forest, and that it was watching the movement rather than driving the animals. Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy has convened a meeting of elected representatives and senior officials in Bengaluru on November 30.
keyFacts: Nayana Motamma submitted her resignation to the Speaker's office on Monday; it has not been accepted.
38 elephants entered Mudigere taluk, split into two groups about 2-3 km apart.
The operation involves over 350 staff, 12 kumkis and more than 100 police personnel.
Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy has called a meeting of MLAs and officials on November 30.
stories.background: Wild elephants have been reported in parts of Hassan since the 1980s. According to earlier reports cited by The Hindu, 24 people have died in elephant attacks in the district since 2020-21. Hassan's forest area of 46,017 hectares is divided into 97 blocks, and the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary has a core area of 49,246 hectares.
stories.whyItMatters: Residents of Mudigere and nearby taluks face the prospect of the herds staying near farmland and coffee estates, while Hassan villagers have faced deaths and crop losses from the same animals.

stories.headline: Karnataka forest department proposes 10 green spaces around Bengaluru, with ₹10 entry
stories.dek: The plan, expected before the Cabinet on November 30, would open only part of the forest land to the public and keep the rest for conservation.
stories.summary: The Karnataka Forest Department has proposed 10 parks with trails and restored habitats in and around Bengaluru, to go before the Cabinet on November 30. The Times of India and The Hindu report different acreage and cost figures.
body: The Karnataka Forest Department has proposed developing 10 green spaces on forest land in and around Bengaluru, with a plan expected to go before the State Cabinet on November 30, according to The Times of India and The Hindu.

The two outlets report different totals. The Times of India says the plan covers 3,453 acres at a cost of ₹150 crore, funded mainly through corporate social responsibility (CSR) and corporate environmental responsibility (CER) funds. The Hindu, citing the proposal, says it covers 3,271 acres at an indicative cost of ₹222 crore, and seeks in-principle approval. The Hindu also refers to nine locations for the 3,271 acres.

The Times of India reports that entry to all sites would cost ₹10 per person. A forest department official told the paper that gate collections would pay for daily maintenance, and that no decision had been taken on allowing commercial activity such as food stalls. The Hindu, citing the proposal, says ticket revenue would be retained for each park's maintenance.

Only part of the land would be opened to visitors. The Times of India says 1,172 of the 3,453 acres would be accessible and 2,281 acres would stay protected. At Turahalli minor forest, 78 acres would be opened and 519 acres would be an eco-protected zone. The Hindu says 1,303 of 3,271 acres would be opened, with 1,968 acres set aside for restoration and conservation.

The sites include two forest blocks at Turahalli, the Kalkere Forest Ecology Centre inside Bannerghatta National Park, the Doresanipalya research and extension centre, Marasandra, Mandur, Panathur and two blocks at Jarakabande. The Times of India also lists the Madappanahalli biodiversity park.

Planned features include walking, trekking and cycling trails, seating, information panels and eco-friendly toilets, according to The Times of India. The Hindu adds thematic tree plantations, medicinal plant gardens and spaces for environmental education. Both report grassland development.

The Hindu says the proposal would remove eucalyptus and acacia plantations and replace them with indigenous species, but only after the relevant work plans are approved. It lists goals including biodiversity conservation, groundwater recharge and reducing the urban heat island effect.

Jarakabande gets the largest allocation in both reports: ₹35.6 crore according to The Times of India, and over ₹35 crore for the A Block tree cultivation centre according to The Hindu. The Hindu puts Kalkere at ₹21.91 crore and each Turahalli project at over ₹16 crore.

Forest Minister Ramalinga Reddy said the department hoped to finish all 10 parks within a year. He told The Hindu that Bengaluru, with over one crore people, lacked enough parks and green spaces. The Times of India quotes him as saying: "We intend to cash in on the potential of environmental tourism."

After in-principle approval, the department will prepare detailed project reports for each site and seek administrative approval with the Finance Department's concurrence, The Hindu reports. Funding would be phased from 2026-27 through State Budget allocations and CSR funds.
keyFacts: The plan is expected before the Karnataka Cabinet on November 30.
Entry is proposed at ₹10 per person, per The Times of India.
Jarakabande has the largest allocation, over ₹35 crore in both reports.
Reported totals differ: 3,453 acres and ₹150 crore, or 3,271 acres and ₹222 crore.
Minister Ramalinga Reddy said work could finish within a year.
stories.background: The Madappanahalli biodiversity park is listed in the proposal. The Times of India says the previous Siddaramaiah government cleared it. The Hindu says the 154-acre Vishwaguru Basavanna Biodiversity Park received Cabinet approval in January, with initial funding of ₹50 crore, during Eshwar Khandre's tenure as Forest Minister.
stories.whyItMatters: If approved, parts of forest land around Bengaluru would open to the public for a fee, while larger portions would be reserved for restoration.

stories.headline: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok-generated sexual deepfakes
stories.dek: The two states say the company failed to build safeguards against child sexual abuse material and falsely presented Grok and X as safe; SpaceX says it acts against users who try to evade its controls.
stories.summary: Oregon and Virginia have filed separate state-court lawsuits against SpaceX, which now owns xAI, over sexualised deepfakes made with Grok and shared on X. They seek injunctions, civil penalties and other remedies.
body: Oregon and Virginia have sued SpaceX in separate state-court complaints, alleging the company failed to stop users of its Grok AI image generator and the X social network from creating and sharing sexualised deepfakes, including alleged child sexual abuse material.

Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield filed in Multnomah County Circuit Court on Sunday evening. Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones filed in the City of Richmond Circuit Court on Monday morning. As of early Monday, both suits awaited acceptance by the courts, CNBC reported.

CNBC said the two are the first states to sue the company over Grok's image generator. The complaints also allege that SpaceX falsely portrayed Grok and X as generally safe, which the states say violates Virginia's Consumer Protection Act and Oregon's Unlawful Trade Practices Act. X allows users aged 13 and older.
Both states seek injunctions, civil penalties, disgorgement and legal costs. Virginia also seeks restitution for consumers.

Al Jazeera reported that the suits accuse the company of promoting Grok's "spicy mode". Ars Technica reported that X says every Grok output is screened, while the state attorneys general say Grok is still producing such material.

Jones wrote that the content "can cause fear, distress, and anxiety in those who are unwillingly exposed to the content." Rayfield wrote that such conduct "erodes important norms regarding consent and privacy and trivializes sexual imagery, abuse, and exploitation."

In a statement from a SpaceXSI spokesperson, also posted on the @Safety account on X, the company said: "When someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content, we take appropriate measures, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement." It said those who try to create such material should be prosecuted.
At a New York City Council hearing in October, SpaceX AI policy leader Gabriela Castillo Madrid said the company had "safeguards" and "strict controls" around its AI products.

SpaceX already faces other Grok- and X-related lawsuits and government probes, including in the U.K., Spain, Ireland, France and California. When Baltimore sued xAI, the company argued that Section 230, a federal law that largely shields platforms from liability for user content, protected it. In a federal case in Texas against a user, SpaceX's lawyers described Grok as "a neutral tool, subject to user control."
keyFacts: Oregon filed on Sunday evening; Virginia filed on Monday morning.
Both states seek injunctions, civil penalties, disgorgement and legal costs.
Virginia also seeks restitution for consumers.
Both suits were awaiting court acceptance as of early Monday, CNBC reported.
Authorities in the U.K., Spain, Ireland, France and California have also probed Grok and X.
stories.background:
Research by the Internet Watch Foundation, the Center for Countering Digital Hate and others found that versions of Grok and X enabled explicit deepfakes based on real photos or videos of children and non-consenting adults, CNBC reported. xAI is now owned and operated by SpaceX.

State attorneys general have recently won changes from social media firms. In August, Meta settled a federal case without admitting wrongdoing, agreeing to pay states around $17 billion over 10 years and to change its apps.
stories.whyItMatters: The suits test whether state consumer-protection law can be used to force changes to an AI image generator and the platform that distributes its output, with minors among those potentially affected.

stories.headline: CII asks government for regulatory transparency after Modi presses industry on investment
stories.dek: Senior CII officials said clearer rules and market integrity would draw private capital, days after the prime minister criticised companies at a Ficci meeting.
stories.summary: The Confederation of Indian Industry outlined steps to boost private investment, including regulatory transparency and easier cross-border capital flows. The statements followed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's criticism of industry at Ficci's annual general meeting last week.
body: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) on Monday asked the government to strengthen market integrity, improve regulatory transparency and ease cross-border capital flows, days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi criticised Indian industry at a Ficci meeting.

Addressing the annual general meeting of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry last week, Modi faulted companies for continued reliance on imports in critical sectors. He said they treated the vast domestic market as a "comfort zone" instead of improving product quality and building capabilities to compete globally. Business Standard also reported that he criticised industry for falling short on job creation.

CII Director General Chandrajit Banerjee said in a post on X that the government's key strategy must be to create a business environment with strong investor protection, regulatory ease and market integrity. He said regulators should ensure their compliance requirements do not obstruct the free flow of cross-border capital. He described Modi's call to invest more, innovate and improve competitiveness as a strong reminder of the need to raise productivity.

Rajiv Memani, CII's immediate past president, said global investors wanted rules that were clear, predictable and proportionate. India, he said, would need both domestic savings and foreign capital to finance its investment needs. He added that openness to global capital and market integrity were complementary objectives.

Sanjiv Puri, a former CII president and chairman and managing director of ITC, said strong corporate governance and predictable regulation were essential to attract long-term capital. R Dinesh, another former president and executive chairman of TVS Supply Chain Solutions, said clear rules, strong governance and proportionate regulation could help deliver access to capital and confidence in market oversight.

CII President R Mukundan, managing director and chief executive officer of Tata Chemicals, said the next priority was to move from ease of doing business to the "speed of doing business". He said CII's Private Investment Barometer showed private project announcements reached a record ₹26.6 trillion in the first half of FY27, 4.4 times the long-run average.

Headlines from The Quint and NDTV on Monday also covered the exchange. The Quint framed Modi's remarks as a question about the pay-off from government support to industry. NDTV reported that Congress MP Shashi Tharoor backed the prime minister on corporate pay and then criticised the Centre over jobs. The full texts of those reports were not available.
Mukundan said the task now was for industry to make "India First" the basis of every long-term decision, and that CII and its members were committed to that agenda.
keyFacts: CII officials spoke on Monday, November 23, after Modi's Ficci address last week.
Private project announcements hit ₹26.6 trillion in H1 FY27, CII said.
That figure is 4.4 times the long-run average, according to R Mukundan.
Shashi Tharoor backed Modi on corporate pay but criticised the Centre on jobs, NDTV reported.
stories.background: Modi spoke at Ficci's annual general meeting last week. According to Business Standard, he criticised companies for relying on imports in critical sectors and for treating the domestic market as a comfort zone.
stories.whyItMatters: Industry's call for clearer, more predictable regulation bears on how much private investment flows into infrastructure, logistics and other sectors.

stories.headline: Tata Steel buys ₹5,825-crore APL Apollo stake; shares of both firms fall
stories.dek: Tata Steel fell 8.2% and APL Apollo Tubes 21.4% on Monday, together losing ₹30,707 crore in market value, as analysts questioned the deal's structure and debt.
stories.summary: Tata Steel bought 2.77 crore APL Apollo Tubes shares worth about ₹5,825 crore in a block deal on Monday. Shares of both companies fell sharply, and together they lost ₹30,707 crore in market value.
body: Tata Steel on Monday bought 2,77,38,075 shares of APL Apollo Tubes, worth about ₹5,825 crore, in a block deal from promoter group entity S Gupta Holding Private Limited, according to BSE block deal data.

The shares were priced at ₹2,100 each. APL Apollo Tubes closed at ₹1,668.15 on Monday, down 21.39% from its previous close of ₹2,122.15. Business Standard reported that Tata Steel fell nearly 8.2%, the biggest percentage loss among Sensex and Nifty 50 stocks, and that APL Apollo was the worst-performing midcap stock. Together the two lost ₹30,707 crore in market value.

In an exchange filing, APL Apollo said its board had approved the company joining a share purchase agreement dated November 23, 2026, with S Gupta Holding and Tata Steel. S Gupta Holding will sell its entire 7,38,60,062 shares, or 26.38% on a fully diluted basis, in three tranches at ₹2,100 a share. The second tranche is 3,33,19,009 shares and the third is 1,28,02,978 shares.

APL Apollo said it is neither buyer nor seller under the agreement and no consideration is payable to or by it. Tata Steel must then make an open offer for up to 7,28,06,387 shares, or 26% of the expanded voting capital, at ₹2,301.40 per share.

Business Standard reported a two-part structure. In the first leg, APL Apollo would buy Tata Steel's tubes and colour-coated businesses for ₹28,000 crore, funded by borrowings. In the second, Tata Steel would take majority control of the enlarged APL Apollo for around ₹32,267 crore. APL Apollo's investor presentation put the deal at about 24.8 times projected FY27 enterprise value to EBITDA.

Bankers cited by Business Standard estimated annual interest of ₹2,800-3,900 crore on the ₹28,000 crore loan, assuming borrowing costs of 10-14 per cent. APL Apollo reported EBITDA of ₹1,914 crore in FY26. Tata Steel's consolidated gross debt was ₹1.02 trillion at the end of September, and its liabilities are expected to rise by about ₹4,200 crore in the first leg.

Shriram Subramanian of InGovern Research Services said the deal did not seem beneficial to either company's shareholders. He said the promoters stood to gain from the sale proceeds and from a contract manufacturing business supplying Tata Steel. The Sanjay Gupta family is set to receive around ₹15,510 crore for its 26.6 per cent stake, the report said.

Amit Tandon of Institutional Investor Advisory Services India questioned why Tata Steel would rely on a contract manufacturer for colour-coated products. He also said that, in his reading of the Companies Act, minority shareholders of neither company would get a vote on the deal.
keyFacts: Tata Steel bought 2,77,38,075 APL Apollo shares at ₹2,100 each on Monday.
APL Apollo closed down 21.39% at ₹1,668.15; Tata Steel fell nearly 8.2%.
Combined market value lost by the two companies: ₹30,707 crore.
Tata Steel's open offer is priced at ₹2,301.40 per share for up to 26%.
APL Apollo expects to raise about ₹28,000 crore in debt.
stories.background: S Gupta Holding held 26.60% of APL Apollo Tubes at the end of the September quarter of FY27. The agreement provides for it to sell its entire holding to Tata Steel in three tranches, the first through the exchange block deal window.
stories.whyItMatters: The deal would add debt at both companies and, if APL Apollo becomes a Tata Steel subsidiary, its borrowings would appear in Tata Steel's consolidated debt. Minority shareholders face an open offer at ₹2,301.40 per share.

stories.headline: ICMR survey finds anaemia prevalence lower than earlier national estimates
stories.dek: The SAMPADA survey, released on Monday, found severe anaemia in under 2% of most age groups, with mild cases making up a large share of the burden.
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research released its SAMPADA 2023-2025 survey on Monday, reporting lower anaemia prevalence than previous national surveys. Severe anaemia affected less than 2% of people in most age groups, and iron deficiency explained about half of cases in women and children.
body: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) reported on Monday, November 23, that anaemia prevalence in its new national survey is lower than in earlier national surveys, with severe anaemia found in less than 2% of people in most age groups.

The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) 2023-2025 covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories. More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed for haemoglobin.

Anaemia prevalence was 42% among children aged 12-59 months and 46% among adolescent girls aged 10-19 years. It was 56% among women of reproductive age. Among adolescent boys aged 10-19 years and men aged 20-59 years, it was 22-23%.

About half of anaemic women, adolescent girls and children have mild anaemia, the report said. Among adolescent boys and adult and older men, three-fourths of those affected have only mild anaemia, according to a release from the Union Health Ministry.

The survey used venous blood sampling and automated analysers to estimate haemoglobin. The release called this the gold standard method. In a sub-sample, researchers also assessed iron, folate and vitamin B12 status, along with the inflammatory markers C-reactive protein and alpha-1-acid glycoprotein.

Iron deficiency accounts for about half of anaemia cases in women, adolescent girls and children, the report said. It is largely restricted to under-five children, adolescent girls and women of reproductive age. Adolescent boys, men and older people showed low prevalence. The report said other causes include infections, haemoglobinopathies and inflammation related to chronic disease.

Vitamin B12 and folate deficiency were similar in anaemic and non-anaemic people across groups, indicating a limited contribution to anaemia in India, the report said. People with moderate and severe anaemia have a high prevalence of iron deficiency and need testing, treatment and tracking until resolution, as envisaged in Anaemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) 2.0, it added.
Rajiv Bahl, secretary of the Department of Health Research, said: "It is encouraging that prevalence of anaemia is lower in SAMPADA compared to previous national surveys."
Bharati Kulkarni, director of ICMR-NIN, said the findings support "more targeted, population-specific and life-course approaches to anaemia prevention and management".
keyFacts: SAMPADA 2023-2025 was released on November 23, 2026.
Survey covered over 2 lakh people in 81,000 households across 183 districts.
Anaemia prevalence among women of reproductive age was 56%.
Iron deficiency accounts for about half of anaemia in women, girls and children.
More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed for haemoglobin.
stories.background: Anaemia Mukt Bharat is the national programme to reduce anaemia. The report said its findings can inform AMB 2.0, which envisages testing and treatment of moderate and severe cases.
stories.whyItMatters: The findings point to iron deficiency as a major but not sole cause, and the report says approaches should target women, adolescent girls and young children and address infections and chronic inflammation as well.

stories.headline: CMC Vellore and TIFR unveil India's first human metabolic chamber
stories.dek: The airtight, live-in laboratory will track how the body uses energy over 24 hours, to study diabetes and obesity among Indians.
stories.summary: The Christian Medical College in Vellore and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research unveiled India's first human metabolic chamber on Monday. Volunteers will live in it for a full day while scientists measure their energy use.
body: The Christian Medical College (CMC) in Vellore and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) on Monday unveiled what they described as India's first Human Metabolic Chamber, a facility for research on metabolism, nutrition, diabetes and obesity.

Punya Salila Srivastava, secretary in the Union health and family welfare ministry, inaugurated the chamber. It was set up jointly by CMC and the Metabolism, Development and Aging (ARUMDA) programme of TIFR.

The chamber is an airtight room with a bed, a desk and a toilet. Volunteers will stay inside for 24 hours, working, resting, eating and sleeping, while scientists monitor them. Meals will be passed in through an airlock.

Researchers will measure oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide output to calculate energy burned during sleep, rest, digestion and physical activity. Scientists call the device a whole-room indirect calorimeter. It will show how the body switches between fat and carbohydrate across meals, activity and sleep, and how metabolism responds to a given diet, meal, medicine, activity level or sleep pattern.

Most metabolic tests capture a snapshot of 20 to 30 minutes, often through a face mask. “This lets it detect small but important differences between individuals that shorter tests miss,” said Dr Nihal Thomas, senior professor of endocrinology, diabetes and metabolism at CMC Vellore.

Ullas Kolthur-Seetharam, coordinator and principal investigator of ARUMDA, said the Indian population is under-represented in global metabolic research. He said the chamber will help show how energy use varies across India's diverse populations, diets and lifestyles.

The chamber will also support long-term studies, including a Vellore birth cohort that CMC has followed since 2010–12. A joint ARUMDA–CMC study of that cohort, published in 2026 in The Lancet Regional Health – Southeast Asia, found overweight and obesity nearly tripled between ages seven and nine, while about one in five children remained thin.

Research will focus on obesity, diabetes, ageing, malnutrition and cancer care. Kolthur-Seetharam said it will give new insight into conditions such as lean diabetes and the long-term effects of low birth weight and early undernutrition.

The facility was funded by the department of atomic energy, with corporate social responsibility support from Hindustan Unilever Limited. NUTRIM at Maastricht University gave expert advice, and the Embassy of the Kingdom of Netherlands in India provided network support. The cost of building the chamber was not disclosed.
The team said precise data on energy needs can strengthen the evidence behind national programmes such as POSHAN Abhiyaan and Anaemia Mukt Bharat.
keyFacts: The chamber was unveiled at CMC Vellore on Monday.
Volunteers will stay inside for 24 hours, with meals delivered through an airlock.
Funding came from the department of atomic energy and Hindustan Unilever Limited's CSR support.
The cost of building the chamber was not disclosed.
Most metabolic tests last 20 to 30 minutes, researchers said.
stories.background: The research team said the chamber builds on India's own tradition in calorimetry, including work at St John's Medical College, Bangalore, from the late 1980s. ARUMDA also runs a National Analytical Facility for Nutrition and Metabolism Research, offering metabolomics, body-composition and stable-isotope methods, which researchers said can be linked to the chamber's energy measurements.
stories.whyItMatters: Researchers say the data will help explain why people of similar body weight differ in diabetes and heart disease risk, and support diet advice suited to Indian foods and ways of living.

stories.headline: UN chief urges nations to agree global AI risk framework within a year
stories.dek: Speaking in Barbados, António Guterres said the framework should be principles-based and backed by independent and credible oversight.
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres told a summit in Barbados on Monday that member states should develop a global AI risk-management framework within a year. He suggested shared safety measures, a testing regime and independent oversight as a starting point.
body: UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Monday called on member states to develop, within the next year, a global framework for managing the risks of artificial intelligence, speaking at a summit on the technology in Barbados.

"Today I call for member states to coordinate efforts and to develop within the next year a globally inclusive and principles-based multilateral framework for AI risk management, backed by independent and credible oversight," he said at the Bridgetown Special Summit On AI Safety.
Guterres said a starting point could be for countries to agree on shared safety measures, a testing regime and basic requirements for independent oversight, according to France 24 and AFP.

Asked by AFP about the state of global institutions, he said many of them "correspond to the reality of the world in 1945". He added: "It's clear that institutions need to be reformed in order to adapt themselves to the realities of today's world." He said this applied to the UN, the international financial architecture and the world trade system.

Guterres said he would advise his successor that properly controlling AI is necessary for "humanity to maintain control of our world". The successor is due to take office in the New Year but has not yet been selected.

France 24 reported that international regulation of AI looks difficult while the United States and China compete for an advantage in research and development. It said US regulators, in the country where AI development has moved fastest, are unlikely to intervene.

In September, US President Donald Trump hosted a group of American technology executives who agreed to follow a voluntary code of conduct on AI safety. Also that month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX chief Elon Musk called for a slowdown in AI development. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg want to move ahead at full speed, France 24 reported.
keyFacts: Guterres spoke on Monday at the Bridgetown Special Summit On AI Safety in Barbados.
He asked member states to agree a framework within one year.
He proposed shared safety measures, a testing regime and independent oversight requirements.
His successor is due to take office in the New Year but is yet to be selected.
stories.background: Guterres has become more vocal about AI safety as his term at the UN nears its end, France 24 reported. In September, several technology leaders called for a slowdown in AI development, while others favoured faster progress, and US technology executives agreed to a voluntary code of conduct.
stories.whyItMatters: A binding international framework would affect how governments and companies test and oversee AI systems, though France 24 notes the US and China are competing for a lead in the technology.

stories.headline: New Zealand bat out final day to draw Wellington Test with India
stories.dek: Captain Shubman Gill called the Basin Reserve surface "not a great Test wicket" after India, on 720 for 9 declared, took only five second-innings wickets.
stories.summary: New Zealand finished on 239 for 5 after 120 overs on the final day, and the captains shook hands to end the first Test at the Basin Reserve. Gill criticised the pitch, saying it got flatter and slower.
body: New Zealand batted out the final day of the first Test against India at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Monday, finishing on 239 for 5 in their second innings when the captains shook hands for a draw.

India began the day needing eight wickets. They declared their first innings at 720 for 9 and New Zealand had made 368, so the hosts still trailed by 113 runs at the end. Fifteen of the scheduled overs were left unbowled.

Overnight batters Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra were separated in the morning. Washington Sundar had Conway for 65 when an inside edge lobbed off the pad to Rishabh Pant. Prasidh Krishna then had Ravindra for 37, caught by KL Rahul at second slip.
Anshul Kamboj removed Tom Blundell for 15 just before the new ball, a decision confirmed on review after Pant had not heard the edge. That left New Zealand at 176 for 5.
Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips then batted together for 43 overs. Mitchell was unbeaten on 49 from 186 balls and Phillips on 26 from 126, adding 63 for the sixth wicket.

India had chances. Akash Deep fumbled at mid-on and missed a run-out against Mitchell, and Devdutt Padikkal could not hold a gloved catch at forward short leg. Jasprit Bumrah bowled in short spells, finishing with 1 for 42 from 20 overs on the day.

Gill criticised the surface after the match. "On Day(s) 3, 4, and 5, it just went flatter and flatter," he said. "The wicket just got slower, so having seen that, I think it was not a great Test wicket, especially if you want results."

Gill also said draws had become less common in recent years, which made the frustration greater. India's captain said that if the team won five of its next six Tests, it should be in a good position to qualify for the World Test Championship final.

New Zealand's Henry Nicholls said it was "a great Test match" and that a draw "from where we were was a pleasing result." Nicholls made 175 not out in the first innings, adding 216 for the sixth wicket with Phillips, who scored 118.
The second Test starts in Christchurch on Friday.
keyFacts: New Zealand finished on 239 for 5 after 120 overs; India had declared at 720 for 9.
Daryl Mitchell made 49 not out and Glenn Phillips 26 not out in a 63-run stand.
Conway scored 65 and Ravindra 37 before falling to Washington Sundar and Prasidh Krishna.
The second Test begins in Christchurch on Friday.
stories.background: India reduced New Zealand to 70 for 5 on the first day, but Nicholls and Phillips added 216 for the sixth wicket to lift the hosts to 368. India's innings of 720 for 9 included centuries from Rahul and Pant, while Gill fell two runs short of one.
stories.whyItMatters: The draw leaves India fourth in the 2025-2027 World Test Championship standings, according to ABC and The Indian Express. New Zealand drop out of the top two.

stories.headline: Marc Marquez wins eighth MotoGP title, equalling Agostini's premier class record
stories.dek: The Ducati rider clinched the 2026 championship at Portimao with one race weekend left, after recovering from a 102-point deficit, the largest overcome in MotoGP history.
stories.summary: Marc Marquez won the 2026 MotoGP world championship in Portugal on Sunday, his eighth premier class title, level with Giacomo Agostini. He overcame a 102-point deficit, the biggest recovered in the sport's history, according to BBC Sport.
body: Spain's Marc Marquez won the 2026 MotoGP world championship at Portimao in Portugal on Sunday, securing his eighth premier class title and drawing level with Italy's Giacomo Agostini, with one race weekend still to run in Valencia.

Marquez, a Ducati rider, overcame a 102-point deficit to take the title, the largest in MotoGP history, according to BBC Sport. He had twice missed the chance to clinch it earlier, in Qatar and in Saturday's sprint race in the Algarve.

His season began without a win. He arrived at the French Grand Prix in May winless, then crashed in the sprint at Le Mans and needed operations on his foot and shoulder. He missed the next round in Barcelona and returned at Mugello 20 days later, trailing the leader Marco Bezzecchi.

"In that moment after the crash in Le Mans and then the seventh surgery on the right shoulder, [my title charge] was completely over," Marquez told BBC Sport. He then won seven of the next 13 grand prix races.

Agostini, 84, who won his eight premier class titles between 1966 and 1975, surprised Marquez on stage in Portugal and presented him with a golden helmet. "It is a big pleasure to equal Giacomo Agostini in premier class titles," Marquez said. "He is the greatest of all time."

Marquez, aged 33 years and 278 days, is the oldest MotoGP champion of the modern era. The title is his 10th world championship across all classes, after wins in 125cc and Moto2. That is one more than Valentino Rossi, who has nine.

At the post-race news conference Marquez referred to that gap, saying: "This championship is for all of my fans, because when they speak at the table at Christmas, 'blah, blah, blah, blah' - 'yeah, yeah, yeah, but 10'."

Asked on Monday whether he is the greatest of all time, Marquez said he was proud when fans and media described him that way but did not agree. "Every athlete in motorsport has their moments, their career and injuries and I respect all of them," he said.
His Ducati contract runs until 2028. The final round of the season is in Valencia.
keyFacts: Marquez clinched the 2026 MotoGP title at Portimao, Portugal, on Sunday.
It is his eighth premier class title, equalling Giacomo Agostini.
He overcame a 102-point deficit, the largest in MotoGP history.
Marquez has 10 world titles overall; Valentino Rossi has nine.
Rossi holds 89 premier class wins; Marquez has 80.
stories.background:
Marquez won six titles with Honda between 2013 and 2019, then went six years without one after repeated injuries. He left Honda after finishing 14th in 2023, joined Gresini Racing, then moved to the factory Ducati team and won the 2025 title.

His rivalry with Rossi included a 2015 collision at Sepang that led to a back-of-the-grid penalty for Rossi, who has said Marquez deliberately sabotaged his title hopes.
stories.whyItMatters: Marquez now matches the premier class title record held by Agostini, and the result renews discussion of who is the sport's greatest rider.

stories.headline: Alcaraz beats Zverev in straight sets to win ATP Finals in Turin
stories.dek: The Spaniard becomes the first from his country to win the season-ending title since Alex Corretja in 1998, according to Sportstar.
stories.summary: Carlos Alcaraz beat Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 (7) in the ATP Finals title match in Turin. He joins Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic as men who have won all four Grand Slams and the event.
body: Carlos Alcaraz defeated Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 (7) in the final of the ATP Finals in Turin, winning the season-ending title after a year interrupted by injury.
Sportstar reported the match was played on Sunday, November 23. The Indian Express carried an AP photo caption dated November 22. The match score is the same in both reports.

Zverev had not dropped a service game in the tournament before the final. He saved three break points in the opening game but was broken two games later, and Alcaraz moved through the first set quickly, according to Sportstar. The Indian Express said Alcaraz broke Zverev three times in the first set and once in the second.

The second set was closer, with both players exchanging breaks. Alcaraz went 3-0 up in the tiebreak before Zverev won six points in a row. Alcaraz then saved three set points, set up a mini-break and closed out the match at his second match point with a drop shot, Sportstar said.

Alcaraz said afterwards: "It's been an amazing week. I couldn't finish the week in a better way, so I'm really proud." He added: "I've been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team, and we could go through everything."
Sportstar said he had a hamstring issue earlier in the tournament. It also said he spent several months out with injury this year. The Indian Express described his return as following a wrist injury.

Zverev, 29, reached the final with straight-set wins over Ben Shelton, Daniil Medvedev, Arthur Fils and Rafael Jodar, according to The Indian Express. He ends 2026 as world No. 1 after winning the US Open and French Open.
The Indian Express said Zverev called Alcaraz "an absolute legend at only 23 years old" and added: "If you retire tomorrow, it's okay! Just relax."
The Indian Express reported that Alcaraz has beaten Zverev in five of their previous six meetings and has won six titles this year. Jannik Sinner also won six.
keyFacts: Alcaraz won the ATP Finals final 6-2, 7-6 (7) in Turin.
He is the first Spaniard to win the event since Alex Corretja in 1998.
Zverev had not lost a service game before the final.
Alcaraz joins Federer, Agassi and Djokovic as winners of all four Slams and the ATP Finals.
Zverev ends 2026 as world No. 1, having won the US Open and French Open.
stories.background: Zverev became world No. 1 this year, a position The Indian Express said was helped by long injury absences for Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner. The newspaper said Zverev's 69-19 record is the lowest win percentage for a year-end men's No. 1 this century.
stories.whyItMatters: The result gives Alcaraz a title to end a year disrupted by injury and adds the ATP Finals to his Grand Slam wins. Zverev holds the year-end No. 1 ranking but lost the decisive match.

stories.headline: FIFA confirms US-led 2031 and UK 2035 Women's World Cup hosts
stories.dek: Both bids were uncontested; the 2031 finals will be the first Women's World Cup with 48 teams, and the UK stages its first World Cup since 1966.
stories.summary: FIFA's Congress approved the joint US, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica bid for 2031 and the four-nation UK bid for 2035 at a special virtual meeting on Monday. Each was the only bid submitted.
body: FIFA confirmed on Monday that the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host the 2031 Women's World Cup, and that England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will jointly host the 2035 edition.

The hosts were ratified at a specially arranged virtual meeting of FIFA's Congress from its Zurich headquarters. Both bids were uncontested, and FIFA President Gianni Infantino had said last year that neither faced a rival, according to DW.

The 2031 tournament will be the first Women's World Cup with 48 teams. The US has hosted the event twice before, in 1999 and 2003, and has won it four times. Emily Cosler, US Soccer's vice-president of strategy, told The Guardian: "We expect and plan for the 2031 Women's World Cup to be the largest women's sporting event in history."
The 2035 tournament will have 104 matches between 48 teams over 39 days, BBC News reported. It will be the first World Cup in the UK since the men's tournament in 1966.

The "All Together" bid proposed 19 venues: 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales. Three more grounds could be added, taking the total to 22 venues in 16 cities. The Guardian reported that the list is expected to be cut to about 16.

FIFA's evaluation, published earlier this month, rated the bid 4.3 out of five and its contractual framework "medium risk". It said certain government guarantees, particularly on tax and safety and security, contained qualifications. BBC News said this is thought to refer to a FIFA request for tax-free status for football-related activities. FIFA said the long lead-in time provided "a sound basis" for resolving the issues.
FIFA has not yet decided whether all four UK co-hosts will qualify automatically.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the tournament would bring "visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country". Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said hosting would allow the FA to build on the legacy of Euro 2022 "across all four nations".
The next Women's World Cup is in Brazil in 2027, from June 24 to July 25. Eighteen of its 32 teams have qualified.
keyFacts: 2031 hosts: United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica; first 48-team Women's World Cup.
2035 hosts: England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, with 104 matches over 39 days.
Both bids were uncontested and ratified at a virtual FIFA Congress on Monday.
FIFA rated the UK bid 4.3 out of five and its contract framework 'medium risk'.
The 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil runs from June 24 to July 25.
stories.background: The UK last hosted a World Cup in 1966. England staged the Women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won, and England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the men's European Championship in 2028. Northern Ireland missed out on 2028 after the UK government said in 2024 it would not fund Casement Park's redevelopment; a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage 2035 matches.
stories.whyItMatters: The awards fix hosts for the next two editions after 2027 and set the 48-team format for the women's tournament. Outstanding tax and security guarantees in the UK bid remain subject to further discussion with FIFA.
